text:
carol: Quick sync — we need to align OTel attributes -> Prom labels for the new runtime dashboards (routing, quotas, rollouts UX). Main concern: high-cardinality labels blowing up Prom. Can we decide here so I can start a short PR?

matt: +1 to a small doc first. My high-level proposal: canonical labels = service, env, model_family, model_variant, route, rollout_group, priority. Keep anything customer-specific out unless it's aggregated (customer_tier) or hashed_client_id for debug only.

sophie: For latency/throughput histograms we also want an input_size bucket (short/med/long) or seq_len_bucket, but that adds cardinality. Maybe we emit a separate histogram tagged only by route and model_family and use logs/traces for finer slices.

ray: Agree with keeping Prom lean. Avoid dynamic labels like model_revision_sha or user_id in Prom. Map those to logs / tracing. If we need "version" in dashboards, use a recorded metric that maps model_revision -> model_tag (low cardinality).

maya: From product — we do need per-customer quota dashboards for enterprise customers. Proposal: publish customer_tier (free, pro, enterprise) for dashboards and expose hashed_cid only in an internal-only metric with retention 7d for debugging.

carol: Quick naming conv question: snake_case for Prom labels or kebab? I'd vote snake_case (prom convention). Example labels: service, env, model_family, model_variant, route, rollout_group, seq_len_bucket, customer_tier.

matt: snake_case SGTM. Example metric (for the doc):

```
# TYPE redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds histogram
redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="runtime",env="prod",model_family="gptj",model_variant="gptj-6b-8bit",route="/v1/generate",seq_len_bucket="short"} 42
redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_sum{service="runtime",env="prod",model_family="gptj",model_variant="gptj-6b-8bit",route="/v1/generate"} 12.34
redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_count{service="runtime",env="prod",model_family="gptj",model_variant="gptj-6b-8bit",route="/v1/generate"} 200
```

sophie: That example is helpful. But note model_variant has ~30 values today and route ~200. If we add seq_len_bucket=10 we multiply cardinality. We should only include seq_len_bucket in a separate metric or limit seq_len_bucket to 3( short, med, long ).

ray: Cardinality calc: service(3) * env(3) * model_family(20) * model_variant(30) * route(200) * rollout_group(5) = huge. We must be intentional and prefer separate metrics keyed by a smaller subset. Also consider relabeling rules to drop model_variant for long-tail routes.

matt: Also: OTel mapping proposal: span.attr service.name -> prom label service, resource.attributes redwood.model -> model_family, resource.attributes redwood.model.variant -> model_variant, http.route -> route, feature.rollout.group -> rollout_group. Document this mapping and add examples.

carol: OK next steps: 1) matt will open a short RFC/PR with canonical label list + mapping examples (OTel->Prom) and recommended low-card grouping patterns; 2) ray will draft Prom recording rules / relabel configs to collapse high-cardinality into buckets or drop in ingestion; 3) maya will supply customer_tier bucket definitions and list of enterprise customer ids for the internal-only hashed metric; 4) sophie will prototype separate histograms for input_size with 3 buckets. Aim: PR + configs merged by next Thu so dashboards can be rebuilt. :thumbsup:
